regressor_basis: The published capitalisation-weighted index of the exchange the share is listed on — the local index the beta rule asks for, resolved from that exchange by the routine rather than chosen by the study.
unused_note: The index series ends 2026-07-24, before the last stock session used elsewhere in the study (2026-08-07). 2 weekly stock observations therefore fall outside the regression. The window stops where the index stops rather than pairing the stock against a stale index level.
composite_basis: ADX-listed names in the UAE library
window_note: The stock listed on 02-Jun-2023 and the index series ends before its last session, so the regression window runs 2023-06-16 to 2026-07-17 — 3.09 years, short of the five-year target, which no amount of method can create.
lead_lag: The estimate is a lead-lag sum beta: the routine regresses on one lag, the contemporaneous return and one lead and sums the three slopes, so the co-movement a thinly traded share books late is already inside the adopted figure rather than published beside it as a separate correction.
blume_note: Blume shrinkage on the adopted slope — two-thirds of the measured figure plus one-third of 1.0, the standard adjustment for the tendency of a measured beta to drift toward the market over time. It is a cross-check reported by the same record, and it is not what the study discounts at.
weak_reason: R-squared = 18.1% against the 10% weak-instrument threshold; the 90% confidence interval [0.59, 1.62] spans 0.94x the point estimate

adopted.basis: tier-1 own-stock weekly regression against the published index of the share's own exchange, produced by the engine's sanctioned routine
adopted.why: n = 159 weekly observations against the published index of the share's own exchange, resolved by the routine from the exchange the share is listed on, over 2023-06-16 to 2026-07-17. R-squared = 0.181, SE(beta) = 0.315. passes minimum usability gate.
adopted.corroboration: Cross-checked three ways. (i) Shrunk toward the market on the Blume adjustment the same record reports, the slope is 1.069, which sits inside the regression's own 90% interval of [0.59, 1.62] and moves the estimate toward one. (ii) Regressing against an equal-weight composite of the exchange's own names instead of the published index gives 0.690 (R-squared 0.167), and against the wider ADX+DFM library 0.802 (R-squared 0.196). (iii) The sector prior for a listed tanker owner is 0.9-1.4 and for a contracted, fee-based marine services provider 0.5-0.9; the adopted figure is read against both in the study rather than accepted at face value.

composite_variant.note: Equal-weight composite of the exchange's own listed names, the subject excluded. This was the regressor before the published index was available; disclosed so the effect of the change is visible, not adopted.

full_library_variant.note: ADX + DFM equal-weight composite; disclosed, not adopted.

self_inclusion_bias.note: The subject is a constituent of the published index it is regressed against, and on a capitalisation-weighted index that cannot be undone. The equal-weight proxy is run both ways to measure how large the resulting self-covariance is: the two figures here differ by 0.202, which is the scale of the upward pull the published-index beta also carries. It is disclosed rather than assumed away, and it works against the study's own conclusion, since removing it would lower the beta further.

thin_trading.note: Share of sessions closing unchanged, against the median of the UAE library. A high ratio is the documented mechanism for a downward-biased contemporaneous beta.

plausibility.mix_note: Roughly half of group revenue is contracted work for the parent group and half is exposed to spot and short-charter shipping markets, so an estimate between the two priors is the economically coherent answer.
